title: Dedicated: emit burst-capacity metering events (committed vs burst) for billing exports
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Dedicated billing exports can now distinguish committed throughput consumption vs burst usage via new metering events and daily rollups (feature-flagged).
description: Context: Dedicated tiers require billing/usage export to separate committed throughput consumption from burst capacity so Finance/Sales/CS can explain invoices and enforce tier policies (ENG-19302). This PR introduces a canonical metering event for burst usage, wires it into the request accounting path, and adds a daily aggregation job that produces committed_vs_burst totals per deployment_id/model/region. Definitions: (1) committed_usage_tokens = tokens attributed while the deployment is within its committed throughput floor capacity slice, (2) burst_usage_tokens = tokens attributed while the deployment consumes burst pool capacity above its committed slice, (3) unmetered_tokens = tokens excluded from billing exports (e.g., internal health checks, warmup). Attribution is computed at request finalization using the tier-aware admission/routing decision already attached to the request context (pool_assignment + capacity_class). Guardrails: feature flag `metering.dedicated_burst_v1` default off; if the capacity_class tag is missing, we fall back to committed (to avoid under-billing) and emit a counter `metering_burst_missing_capacity_class_total` for cleanup. Also includes unit tests for streaming vs non-streaming to ensure we do not double-count tokens, and adds a small schema version bump for the billing export (new columns) behind `export.schema_version >= 2025_02_25`. Rollout plan: enable flag for 2 internal Dedicated deployments, validate dashboards/export parity for 72h, then expand to beta customers selected by CS; Finance to validate sample invoices before GA.
commit_summary: metering: add CapacityClass enum + attach to metering context
dedicated: emit MeteringEventV3 with committed/burst token counters
billing-export: add schema v2025_02_25 with burst fields behind version gate
jobs: daily rollup for dedicated_usage_committed_tokens and dedicated_usage_burst_tokens
tests: streaming accounting parity + regression for partial chunk retries
docs: internal notes for Finance/CS on interpreting burst columns
illustrative_snippets: New event fields (proto-ish): committed_usage_tokens, burst_usage_tokens, capacity_class (COMMITTED|BURST|UNKNOWN), schema_version
Exporter columns (v2025_02_25): dedicated_committed_tokens, dedicated_burst_tokens, dedicated_burst_pct, dedicated_capacity_class_missing_tokens
review_conversation: Cole Summers: Can we guarantee the capacity_class tag is present on all Dedicated requests? I worry about inconsistent exports if router/gateway drops it. Also please confirm what happens when we see UNKNOWN.

Nadia Rahman (author): Not guaranteed yet (router rollout is staggered). In this PR: if missing/UNKNOWN we default to COMMITTED for billing (conservative) and emit `metering_burst_missing_capacity_class_total` + include `dedicated_capacity_class_missing_tokens` in the export so we can quantify gaps. Follow-up task proposed in ENG-19302 to make capacity_class required once tier-aware routing is GA.

Sean Gallagher: Please document whether burst is defined by admission-control decision or by observed throughput exceeding floor. We should avoid tying this to runtime variability; it needs to be policy-based and auditable.

Nadia Rahman (author): Agreed—this is policy-based. Burst attribution comes from the routing/admission decision (capacity_class) at request start, not from measured tokens/sec. Added a paragraph to the PR description and internal docs and a unit test asserting we never compute burst from observed throughput.
Logan Wright: Any risk of double counting on streaming retries? We had an incident where token accounting was inflated for chunk replays.

Nadia Rahman (author): Added regression coverage for partial chunk retries; we only increment counters on finalization with the canonical token ledger entry (post-dedupe). Also verified against existing `request_token_ledger` invariants. Linked the test case in the PR.
Laura Bennett: For Finance review: will burst tokens show as a separate line item or just a column in the export? And can we compute burst % of total by month?

Nadia Rahman (author): This PR adds export columns; invoicing presentation is handled downstream. The daily rollup includes both counters so monthly aggregation is straightforward. Added an example query in internal docs and a dashboard panel for burst % by deployment.
